Summary and scope ▸

This run exercises the coach-facing report end to end: PIN login as a coach, the assignment-scoped dashboard, the full report at /c2a/coach/students/:id, and the generated PDF. It targets exactly the eight commits that ported and reshaped the coach report on this branch. The scoring pipeline itself is untouched by these commits, so the risk here is presentation and cross-surface parity, which is what the checks below focus on.

No new production data was created. The C2A host has no coach users by design, so the run reused an existing synthetic coach (synth_coach_0819) already assigned to a synthetic student. Nothing was written to the production database during this test.

Notes: two apparent gaps that are not defects ▸

1. Summary shows "Coming soon"

The Summary section is an intentional reserved placeholder for the coach-facing overview. It renders identically in the browser and the PDF. Not introduced by this branch.

2. Applied EF rollup reports "unavailable"

The coach detail response carries an appliedEfRollup that reads a trace_snapshot from c2a_pipeline_audits. That table is written by a separate admin verification step, not by normal scoring.

Production finding (not a branch defect): the c2a_pipeline_audits table is currently empty in production (0 rows), so the applied-EF rollup resolves to "unavailable" for every student, not just synthetic ones. The projection code is byte-identical between the deployed SHA 9e6e85b75 and this branch, so this is a pre-existing production condition. The Engine section still renders fully from the app-owned definitions and the coach language pack. Reaching the populated applied-EF path would require exercising the admin verification flow that writes the audit trace, which is orthogonal to this coach-report UI branch.
